1.
List has been revised.
2. Heard Sri V.M. Zaidi, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Shahjad Alam, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Arun Kumar Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.

3. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 402 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406, 467, 468, 504, 506 of IPC, Police Station Modinagar, District Ghaziabad, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant along with co-accused person Manju Devi are stated to have agreed to enter into an agreement to sell of a land in question for a consideration of Rs.30 Pankaj Saini vs State Of U.P. on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130449396/
1 lakhs which were transferred through RTGS to the account of the applicant and a time of three months was given to execute the sale-deed.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Senior Counsel for the applicant has stated at Bar that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has apprehension of his arrest.
The applicant is a bonafide person.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
Learned Senior Counsel has further stated that the applicant is ready to execute the sale-deed in favour of the informant but the informant does not want to get the land rather wants the money back.
The matter of civil in nature has been converted into a criminal one by the informant by instituting the present FIR.
6. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal history.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

7. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

8. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98", the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

12. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
